subtasks.title: Teach the CI/local ClickHouse substrate about zod.aggregate_kit_camera_name
subtasks.approach: Shared prerequisite for every other node: the driving table is absent from the dump that CI and clickhouse-qa replay, so any query against it fails until this lands. Append ONE translated DDL line to database/schema/clickhouse-schema.sql in zod alphabetical position, add the table to RequiresClickhouse's truncation list so new fixtures do not cross-pollute, and record the table in .claude/commands/chlocal.md as a manually-maintained addition so the next dump regeneration cannot silently drop it. The engine MUST be ReplacingMergeTree(), not production's SharedReplacingMergeTree: the OSS clickhouse-server:26.2 CI image has no Shared* engines, and a verbatim paste fails at dump load and takes the whole ClickHouse CI job down (driver-findings.md sec 2; dump header at database/schema/clickhouse-schema.sql:1-5 states the translation rule; measured zero Shared* engines across 62 CREATE TABLE lines). Already human-approved via prep-context question 6 (append one translated line + record it with the generator) - no new approval needed. TDD: no test of its own; it is what makes t2's and t3's tests able to go red for the right reason instead of erroring on a missing relation.

subtasks.title: Add OrgKitCameraNamesQuery: kit_ids -> camera_name => kit_ids
subtasks.approach: New ClickhouseQuery mirroring OrgKitLastScanQuery's shape and docblock idiom (app/Clickhouse/Queries/OrgKitLastScanQuery.php:14-19, :31-66). handle(['kit_ids' => list<int>]) reads zod.aggregate_kit_camera_name WITH FINAL and inverts kit_id => camera_name into camera_name => list<int> kit_ids. Scoping comes ONLY from the PostgreSQL-derived kit_id list - the table is exactly 2 columns (kit_id Int32, camera_name String), measured, so there is no org_id to filter on and no _peerdb_is_deleted to apply (a CDC soft-delete predicate errors here). FINAL rather than GROUP BY because the whole row is the sort key, so FINAL and SELECT DISTINCT collapse it identically (measured raw 12,414 -> 10,600 both ways) and FINAL matches this repo's ReplacingMergeTree convention. Empty/missing kit_ids short-circuits to [] before touching ClickHouse. No org_id argument at all, so no InvalidArgumentException guard - unlike OrgKitLastScanQuery there is no wiring bug that a zero value could hide. TDD: write tests/Unit/Clickhouse/Queries/OrgKitCameraNamesQueryTest.php first; it must go red (class not found / relation missing) before the query class exists.
subtasks.intended_diffs:
app/Clickhouse/Queries/OrgKitCameraNamesQuery.php (NEW):
  declare(strict_types=1); namespace App\Clickhouse\Queries; extends ClickhouseQuery.
  Minimal docblock (operator preference) carrying only the three load-bearing 'why' notes: (1) kit_ids come from PostgreSQL because this table has NO org_id - 2 columns only - so tenancy cannot be scoped here; (2) FINAL, not a CDC predicate: MV-fed, no _peerdb_* columns; (3) FINAL == SELECT DISTINCT here because the whole row is the sort key.
  public static function handle(array $arguments = []): array with @param array{kit_ids?: list<int>} and @return array<array-key, list<int>> camera_name => kit_ids (array-key, NOT string: PHP casts an all-numeric camera_name to an int key - the same caveat OrgKitReportingStatusQuery's @return already documents for mappings).
  Body:
    $kitIds = array_values(array_unique(array_map('intval', $arguments['kit_ids'] ?? [])));
    if ($kitIds === []) { return []; }
    $placeholders = implode(', ', array_fill(0, count($kitIds), '?'));
    $rows = DB::clickhouse('aggregate_kit_camera_name', 'zod', final: true)
        ->select(['kit_id', 'camera_name'])
        ->whereRaw("kit_id IN ({$placeholders})", $kitIds)
        ->get();
    foreach ($rows as $row) { read $row['kit_id'] ?? $row->kit_id and $row['camera_name'] ?? $row->camera_name (both access styles, matching both sibling classes); skip a blank camera_name; $result[$cameraName][] = (int) $kitId; }
    then array_values(array_unique(...)) each bucket so a duplicated (kit_id, camera_name) pair that FINAL did not merge cannot double-count a kit in the rollup.
  DB::clickhouse's 3rd positional arg is $final (app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:69-74) and appends ' FINAL' only when the driver is clickhouse, so the pgsql test bridge stays syntactically valid.

tests/Unit/Clickhouse/Queries/OrgKitCameraNamesQueryTest.php (NEW): class OrgKitCameraNamesQueryTest extends Tests\TestCase, `use RequiresClickhouse`, #[Group('clickhouse')] per test, private const KIT_ID/OTHER_KIT_ID constants - exactly the sibling shape of OrgKitLastScanQueryTest.php:1-60. Fixtures via DB::connection('public_clickhouse')->table('aggregate_kit_camera_name')->insert([...]). Tests:
  - empty kit_ids returns [] (assertSame)
  - missing kit_ids key returns []
  - one kit with several camera_names produces one entry per camera_name, each holding that kit
  - two kits sharing one camera_name produce a single entry holding both kit ids (the many-to-many inversion AC5 depends on)
  - a kit_id NOT in the requested list never appears (the only tenancy boundary this class has)
  - duplicate identical rows collapse under FINAL to one kit id, not two

subtasks.title: Re-key GlKitsResource to GL identity via Filament ->records() array records
subtasks.approach: The ticket's core change (AC1-AC6). Row identity moves from the Eloquent Kit query onto Filament's ->records() array-record API, following the in-repo precedent app/Filament/Widgets/Client/ClientTable.php:138-141 (records/paginated/defaultPaginationPageOption) and :320-349 (a LengthAwarePaginator built from a filtered, sorted, sliced Collection). Necessary because Eloquent cannot sort a getStateUsing column, and both computed columns must sort (AC3). glKits($orgId) stays the single PostgreSQL tenancy boundary; the new OrgKitCameraNamesQuery inverts its kit ids into GL => kit_ids; the two existing per-kit maps roll up per GL with max() on last scan and best-known-wins on reporting. Reporting rank ascending is Reporting(0) < Not Reporting(1) < Unknown(2), and a GL mixing Not Reporting with Unknown and none Reporting renders Not Reporting (Q3/Q4) - which falls out of taking min() of the per-kit rank. ACCEPTED TRADE-OFF (Q1, Dalton 2026-09-04): a GL-discovery failure renders ZERO rows, a resilience regression versus today's PostgreSQL-sourced rows; reportClickhouseFailure() is kept so the outage still reaches error tracking, and this must be stated in the PR body and Build Record. NO table-level 'unavailable' empty state - explicitly rejected. TDD: rework tests/Filament/Resources/GlKitsResourceTest.php first; the new GL-keyed assertions must go red against the current kit-keyed page before the resource is touched.

Drop the ->getStateUsing() closures: array records resolve state via data_get($record, $name) (vendor/filament/support/src/Concerns/HasCellState.php:151-161), so plain array keys are enough.
   ->recordAction(null)->recordUrl(null)   <-- MANDATORY, and MISSED BY PREP. Resource::configureTable() calls static::table() LAST (vendor/filament/filament/src/Resources/Resource.php:73-83), so nulling them here wins. 2. NEW protected static function glRecords(int $page, int $recordsPerPage, ?string $sortColumn, ?string $sortDirection, ?string $search): LengthAwarePaginator
   $orgId = (int) auth()->user()->org_id;
   $glMap = static::glMap($orgId);
   if ($glMap === null || $glMap === []) { return new LengthAwarePaginator([], 0, $recordsPerPage, $page); }   // Q1: discovery failure and 'owns no GLs' are the same empty table, deliberately
   $kits = static::glKits($orgId)->keyBy('id');
   $lastScans = static::lastScanMap($orgId);   // null => read failed
   $reporting = static::reportingMap($orgId);  // null => read failed
   $owner = (string) (auth()->user()->org?->name ?? '');
   Build rows with collect($glMap)->map(function (array $kitIds, string|int $gl) ... ) producing per GL:
     'gl' => (string) $gl, 'company_owner' => $owner,
     'last_scan' => display string, 'last_scan_sort' => sortable scalar,
     'reporting' => badge string, 'reporting_sort' => (string) rank
   then ->keyBy('gl') so Filament's mapWithKeys defaults __key to the GL string (HasRecords.php:123-134) and tests can address rows by that string.
   last scan rollup: $latest = max over the GL's kit_ids of $lastScans[$kitId] (plain string comparison is safe - OrgKitLastScanQuery returns toString(max(last_scan),'UTC') as fixed-width 'Y-m-d H:i:s', so lexicographic == chronological).
     $lastScans === null  => 'Unknown', sort '2'
     $latest === null     => 'Never',   sort '1'
     otherwise            => Carbon::parse($latest, 'UTC')->timezone(auth()->user()->timezone)->format(config('app.date_format')), sort '0'.$latest
   reporting rollup: rank = min over kit_ids of the per-kit rank, so any Reporting => Reporting, else any Not Reporting => Not Reporting, else Unknown (Q3 + Q4 in one expression). Per-kit rank helper (adapting today's reportingState at :146-161): blank kit_mapping => 2; $reporting === null => 2; array_key_exists(strtolower($kit->kit_mapping), $reporting) ? 0 : 1. Map 0/1/2 back to 'Reporting'/'Not Reporting'/'Unknown'.
   search (Q5, GL stays searchable): if filled($search), filter rows on str_contains(Str::lower($row['gl']), Str::lower($search)) BEFORE sorting, so the paginator total reflects the filtered set.
   sort: $sortKey = match ($sortColumn) { 'last_scan' => 'last_scan_sort', 'reporting' => 'reporting_sort', default => 'gl' }; $direction = $sortDirection === 'desc' ? 'desc' : 'asc'; $rows = $rows->sortBy([[$sortKey, $direction], ['gl', 'asc']]) - the array form gives a deterministic GL tiebreak and preserves the GL keys.
   paginate: $slice = $rows->slice(($page - 1) * $recordsPerPage, $recordsPerPage); return new LengthAwarePaginator($slice, $rows->count(), $recordsPerPage, $page). Keys survive the slice, and resolveTableRecord() reads getRecords()[$key] (vendor/filament/tables/src/Concerns/HasRecords.php:190-191), so keyed access and assertCountTableRecords() (which reads the paginator total, HasRecords.php:270-274) both work.

NEW protected static function glMap(int $orgId): ?array - the third once()-per-$orgId memo, byte-for-byte the same idiom as lastScanMap() at :174-193: capture $orgId in the closure so Onceable::hashFromTrace() keys on it, return [] when the kit list is empty, catch \Throwable -> reportClickhouseFailure('camera-names', $orgId, $e) -> return null. @return array<array-key, list<int>>|null. subtasks.approach: Q2 answer, re-confirmed after the driver established there is NO test-time PostgreSQL bridge to extend (zod.kit_last_scan has no PG migration, local-clickhouse-schema.sql defines only a clarity schema and is hand-applied, CI sets CLICKHOUSE_DRIVER=clickhouse) and after a PG shim migration was explicitly rejected.
